Operator:
    Good morning, and welcome to the Stratosphere Aerospace Corporation Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question during the Q&A session, please press star then 1 on your telephone keypad. A confirmation tone will acknowledge your request. If you are using a webcast, you may submit questions via the portal. Please note this event is being recorded.

    I would now like to turn the conference over to Emily Carter, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
    Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Stratosphere Aerospace Corporation's Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Reynolds, Chief Financial Officer; Sarah Bennett, Chief Operating Officer; Dr. Alex Rivera, Chief Technology Officer; and Lisa Wong, Chief Strategy Officer.

    Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the safe harbor provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Actual results could differ materially due to various risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-K and 10-Q, for a complete discussion of these factors.

Johnathan Hale:
    Thank you, Emily, and good morning. Stratosphere Aerospace delivered a solid performance in Q3, demonstrating the resilience of our business model and the strength of our diversified portfolio across defense, space, and commercial aeronautics. Our priorities remain focused on executing our strategy, driving operational excellence, and delivering value to our shareholders. Today, I'll cover key highlights including the performance of our priority defense programs, major new contract awards, updates on key programs, potential risks and opportunities, revenue and earnings guidance by segment, and backlog growth.

    Starting with the performance of our priority defense programs, which form the cornerstone of our Aeronautics and Missiles & Fire Control segments, these efforts drove 14% year-over-year revenue growth to $2.8 billion in the quarter, with segment operating margins expanding 120 basis points to 13.2%. Our book-to-bill ratio was 1.4x, supporting a record backlog of $52 billion, up 8% from last year, giving us exceptional multi-year visibility in light of ongoing geopolitical tensions and elevated global defense spending.

    On next-generation air dominance platforms, our lead effort is the F-47 Raptor II successor under the NGAD framework. We've hit critical milestones in the Engineering and Manufacturing Development phase, completing digital twin validation for the adaptive cycle engine based on GE Aerospace's XA102 XA100-derived architecture. Ground tests showed 25% improved thrust-to-weight ratios and 30% reduced specific fuel consumption, putting us ahead of schedule for Risk Reduction prototypes by FY25. NGAD-related revenue grew 22% to $450 million, with margins at 12.8%, thanks to efficiencies from our Model-Based Systems Engineering approach that cut traditional CAD/CAE timelines by 15%. We're leveraging this for collaborative combat aircraft integration, with initial drone wingman contracts under the Skyborg follow-on targeting a $15 billion market through 2030.

    In fifth-generation sustainment, the F-35 Lightning II continues as a profitability driver. We delivered 48 jets across Lots 17 and 18, up 12% year-over-year, incorporating TR-3 Block 4 upgrades with advanced electronic warfare suites and Sensor Open Systems Architecture for AI-driven mission data processing. International sales shone with $1.2 billion in Foreign Military Sales to NATO allies, including $600 million for Finland and Poland to bolster Baltic Sea deterrence. Program revenue reached $1.9 billion, up 9%, and we've raised full-year guidance to 185-190 deliveries. Margins stayed at 11.5% despite titanium forging supply challenges, which we addressed via dual-sourcing with domestic mills and a 20% inventory build. Lot 19 negotiations with the DoD are advancing positively, with a $10 billion award expected by year-end, highlighting the program's 1.2x book-to-bill and our shift to a $100 billion-plus service life sustainment phase.

    Hypersonics and precision strike outperformed, too. Our Hypersonic Attack Cruise Missile advanced to Low-Rate Initial Production Lot 1, with three successful end-to-end flight tests from B-52s at Edwards AFB achieving Mach 5+ speeds and 20% CEP improvements through machine learning-optimized guidance. This added $320 million in revenue, up 35% year-over-year, backed by a $4.2 billion backlog from Indo-Pacific funding. The Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missile Extended Range saw 18% volume growth to $550 million from U.S. Air Force and Royal Australian Air Force replenishments post-Ukraine. Margins rose to 15.4% with scaled production at Troy, Alabama, where predictive analytics reduced defect rates by 28%. Middle East tensions spurred $800 million in urgent Patriot GEM-T interceptor awards, strengthening our integrated air and missile defense alongside PAC-3 MSE.

    Uncrewed systems and space resilience capped strong results. The MQ-Next loyal wingman drone family gained a $2.1 billion IDIQ ceiling increase from the Navy's Replicator initiative, with $280 million in Q3 revenue, up 40%, linked to collaborative autonomy demos with F/A-18s and E-2Ds using Collins Aerospace's ARINC 653 partitioning for 5x denser AI swarming. In space, Next-Gen Overhead Persistent Infrared polar satellites completed on-orbit checkout for the first two, offering resilient missile warning with 40% lower size, weight, and power via photonic payloads, driving $410 million in revenue and export potential to AUKUS partners.

    Broader trends show U.S. DoD funding up 6% in the FY25 NDAA to $886 billion, with our programs gaining outsized shares in hypersonics (+28%) and collaborative combat aircraft (+45%). Ukraine attrition boosted munitions like our Stinger successor to $150 million, while Taiwan Strait risks lift Pacific Deterrence Initiative spending. We've derisked 92% of critical Tier 1 suppliers via our Defense Industrial Base Resilience program, cutting lead times 35% despite inflation. We're investing 8.5% of segment revenue, or $240 million, in digital transformation like generative AI for design and a joint venture with Northrop Grumman on hypersonic tooling, targeting 10-12% CAGR and ROIC over 18%. Risks like Continuing Resolutions are buffered by fixed-price expertise and 65% cost-plus backlog.

    Transitioning to major new contract awards and program wins, we're thrilled with over $12.4 billion secured this quarter, a 28% year-over-year increase, lifting funded backlog to a record $68.7 billion, up 15% sequentially. About 62% of this is expected to convert to revenue in the next 24 months.

    In Defense Electronics and Missiles, the standout is our $4.2 billion IDIQ from the U.S. Air Force for next-generation hypersonic boost-glide vehicles under Agile Rapid Global Strike. Building on Phase 2B TRL 7 milestones with proprietary scramjet propulsion co-developed with Aerojet Rocketdyne, we're ramping LRIP at Huntsville, Alabama, for Q4 2025 deliveries. This validates $450 million in FY23 hypersonics R&D and paves the way for endo-atmospheric interceptors. We also won a $2.8 billion FMS contract via the State Department for Precision Strike Missile Increment 2 to a key Eastern European NATO ally, with multi-mode seekers amid 35% regional spending growth per SIPRI. Expected margins are accretive at 14-16% via GaN RF vertical integration.

    For Fixed-Wing Platforms, we're prime on the Navy's $3.1 billion NGAD Family of Systems demonstrator over five years, including CCA drones with AI autonomy and sixth-gen sensor fusion. Digital engineering twins cut wind tunnel risks 40%, aligning with JADC2. Internationally, a $1.5 billion firm-fixed-price award from the Royal Australian Air Force under AUKUS Pillar II for F-35 Block 4 upgrades with DRFM jamming, driven by South China Sea tensions and 7.2% APAC A&D CAGR per Deloitte.

    Space Systems added $850 million in wins: $500 million NASA CLPS for Orion-derived lunar lander avionics supporting Artemis IV, leveraging Gateway HALO radiation-hardened processors; and $350 million multi-launch for smallsat Ka-band phased-array antennas at 1 Gbps LEO broadband. Commercial space growth has our backlog up 42% year-over-year.

    These wins emphasize high-margin tech programs, with 45% international up from 32%, derisking U.S. sequestration via dual-use DEW exports. We've derisked 85% critical rare earths domestically, cutting lead times 25%. We're positioned for GCAP Tempest downselect and NGWS, with $10 billion-plus upside, boosting 2024 guidance to 8-10% organic growth amid $2.2 trillion global defense budgets.

    Now, updates on key programs across fixed-wing, hypersonics, unmanned, missile defense, and space, representing our $28.7 billion backlog up 12% year-over-year from DoD, FMS, and sustainment. We've hit 98% first-pass yield, countering titanium shortages and labor via European dual-sourcing and 15% additive manufacturing expansion for titanium ALD parts.

    The Liberty Eagle Next-Generation Fighter program is on track for LRIP Lot 3 at $2.8 billion in Q4 FY24. 92% digital twin validation via MBSE reduced risks 25%; first captive-carry flight was August 15th from Palmdale with adaptive cycle engine at 20% better SFC than F-35's F135. Delivered 18 Block 2 fuselages YTD, up 30%, unit costs down 8% to $145 million via C919 composites. AUKUS interest could add $1.2 billion; margins at 11.2%.

    Hypersonic Strike Vehicle achieved Mach 8 flight test July 22nd from Vandenberg, third hit exceeding Milestone C threshold. SiC TPS cuts ablation 40%, boosting payload 15% to 1,200 lbs. $1.1 billion FRP Lot 1 awarded; 2.5 units/month at Tucson, costs 12% below CER at $18.7 million. Japan co-production study at $450 million; 14.5% margins.

    SwarmHawk SCA hit CCA swarm demo at Yuma with 24 vehicles, 96% autonomy. $900 million IDIQ for 150 units at $4.2 million/copy, down 22%; UAE potential $300 million. 16.8% margins from software-defined hardware.

    Aegis IAMD delivered 142 effectors YTD, up 18%; SM-3 Block IIA ICBM intercept FTM-45. 95% throughput at Rocket Center; costs down 10% to $12.4 million SM-6. Poland Wisla, Saudi FMS add $750 million; sustainment up 25%; 13.1% margins.

    Orion Sentinel SDA Tranche 2: 100% checkout for 12 sats, 10 Gbps OISL. $2.4 billion Tranche 3; $18,500/kg via PICs. $1.5 billion FY25 awards; 12.4% margins.

    These highlight execution in $886 billion FY25 NDAA, 85% fixed-price-incentive. $1.2 billion cash, 2.1x net debt/EBITDA buffer FORGE delays, inflation.

    On potential risks and opportunities in this $1.1 trillion market growing 5.2% CAGR per Deloitte, our 1.3x Defense/1.1x Commercial book-to-bill and $48 billion backlog provide visibility.

    Opportunities: Defense tailwinds from $886 billion FY24 NDAA; hypersonics $2.4 billion DARPA OTA to 15% revenue/18-20% margins by 2027; BAE Tempest/FCAS $1.2 billion. Missile/Space: GPI $3.5 billion IDIQ, SDA T2TL-Alpha $800 million; AUKUS DEW 12-15% APAC growth. Commercial: 22% QoQ aerostructures to $1.1 billion; eVTOL winglets for Joby by 2025, to 35% revenue by 2026. MBSE/digital twins cut EACs 15%; AM for MRO.

    Risks: Supply chain—titanium +35%, semis; mitigated by 90% dual-sourcing, $250 million inventory (50 bps EBITDA hit). Geopol/regs: ITAR caps 5% APAC, inflation 3.2%; 70% FPI, apprenticeships. Competition: Boeing strikes; $450 million IR&D. Cyber up 28%; CMMC L2. Recession 35% odds trims 300 bps; hedged debt/liquidity.

    FY24 revenue $12.5-13 billion midpoint +9%; Defense ops outweigh commercial 3:1.

    Revenue and earnings guidance reflects F-47 ramp, $849.8 billion FY25 DoD +4.1%, commercial recovery at 78% utilization, titanium +15%, inflation. Raised FY24 consolidated to $92.5-94.5 billion (+8-10% organic), margins 11.2-11.7% (+40 bps) via LEAN+/digital. Book-to-bill 1.15x, $168 billion backlog ($52 billion funded). 2025: $98-102 billion (6-8%), 12.0-12.5%.

    Aeronautics (42%): Q3 $10.2 billion +12%; FY24 $39-40 billion +9% from F-47 Lot 16 (156 aircraft, $82 million flyaway -5%); margins 10.8-11.2% (+50 bps) sustainment $8.5 billion. 2025 $42-44 billion; risk 737 MAX delays.

    Missiles/Defense (28%): Q3 $7.8 billion +18%; FY24 $26.5-27.5 billion +14% hypersonics $4.2 billion, GPI. Margins 14.5-15.0%; Ukraine/AUKUS. 2025 $29-31 billion 15.5%.

    Space (18%): Q3 $4.1 billion +9%; FY24 $17-17.5 billion +7% GPS IIIF, NSSL $2.9 billion. Margins 11.0-11.5%; 2025 $18.5-19.5 billion +9%.

    Mission (12%): Q3 $3.4 billion +11%; FY24 $10.5-11 billion +10% subs/C4ISR. Margins 10.5-11.0%; 2025 $11.5-12 billion.

    Finally, backlog growth: Total $142.3 billion, +$16.8 billion (13.4% sequential, 22.7% YoY)—11th straight double-digit quarter, 1.28x book-to-bill vs. industry 1.1x. Funded 68% ($96.7 billion).

    Defense $98.4 billion +$11.2 billion (12.8%): F-35 Lot 16 $4.5 billion, NGAD $2.8 billion, hypersonics $1.2 billion; sustainment $2.7 billion incl. F-22 $1.1 billion.

    Space/Missile $28.7 billion +$3.1 billion (12.1%): SDA $1.9 billion, GPI $850 million.

    Commercial $15.2 billion +$2.5 billion (19.7%): 737/787 $1.8 billion, 1.45x B2B.

    U.S. $108.6 billion (76%) +11.9%; international $23.4 billion +21.3% (ME +28% Patriot $2.1 billion, Indo-Pac $4.8 billion GCAP $1.4 billion, Europe +14.7%).

    $1.2 billion R&D, MBSE cut NGAD bids 15%; $28-30 billion FY25 revenue, 85-90% conversion. $45 billion pipeline.

    We're excited about NGAD advancements and their potential to establish leadership in next-gen air dominance, fueling future growth. Strong defense demand persists, with commercial aerospace recovering steadily.

Michael Reynolds:
    Thank you, Johnathan. Now, to the financials. In Q3, we reported revenue of $24.5 billion, a 12% increase year-over-year. Diluted earnings per share were $2.85. We maintain a strong balance sheet with $5.2 billion in cash and equivalents. Full-year guidance is unchanged at the raised levels discussed. We're managing costs tightly while investing in growth, and committed to capital returns via dividends and $1 billion in share repurchases this year.

    Specific highlights: Gross margin of 12.5%, up 60 basis points; operating income of $3.1 billion, +15%; free cash flow of $2.8 billion year-to-date.

Sarah Bennett:
    Thank you, Michael. Operationally, supply chain management has improved markedly, enabling higher production rates on programs like F-35 and hypersonics. We've invested in automation, digital twins, and predictive analytics, boosting efficiency and cutting costs by 12% in key facilities. Our LEAN+ initiatives have achieved 98% on-time deliveries, with inventory optimization reducing working capital needs by $400 million.

Dr. Alex Rivera:
    Thank you, Sarah. Technologically, we're advancing next-generation propulsion systems, including adaptive cycle engines with 30% better fuel efficiency and scramjet tech for hypersonics. These innovations, paired with AI-driven autonomy and photonic payloads, provide a competitive edge, positioning us for dominance in NGAD, CCA, and resilient space architectures.

Operator:
    Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. To ask a question, press star then 1. Our first question comes from Josh Klein with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Josh Klein:
    Good morning, team. Can you provide more color on the hypersonics program execution and associated risks?

Johnathan Hale:
    Certainly, Josh. As detailed, hypersonics like HACM and HSV exceeded with multiple Mach 5+ tests and LRIP ramps, revenue up 35% to $320 million backed by $4.2-5.7 billion backlogs from Indo-Pacific and DARPA OTAs. Execution leverages SiC TPS, automated production for costs 12% below targets. Risks like thermal ablation or supplier delays are mitigated by digital twins and multi-sourcing; we're ahead on TRLs with 14.5-15.4% margins, positioning for $10 billion+ market share.

Operator:
    Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez:
    Hi, thanks. I'm curious about revenue guidance for the commercial aeronautics segment and recovery drivers?

Michael Reynolds:
    Maria, great question. Commercial is embedded in Aeronautics at 15% segment mix, guiding FY24 $39-40 billion total with strong pull from Boeing/Airbus ramps—737 MAX wings, 787 composites up 22% QoQ to $1.1 billion orders. Post-pandemic fleet utilization at 78%, IATA 4.7% traffic growth supports 2025 expansion to 35% company-wide revenue. Margins benefit from SAF/eVTOL like Joby winglets; risks like OEM cert delays hedged by dual-sourcing.

Operator:
    Our next question comes from Tom Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Tom Patel:
    Regarding backlog conversion rates and international growth exposure?

Dr. Alex Rivera:
    Tom, backlog conversion is robust at projected 85-90% over 2-3 years from $142.3 billion total, 68% funded. International at $23.4 billion +21.3% YoY—ME Patriot/UAE radars $9.2 billion +28%, Indo-Pac GCAP/AUKUS $4.8 billion—driven by tech like OISL in SDA, AI swarms. Digital transformation ensures high-probability unfunded conversion >90%, de-risking FY25 $28-30 billion revenue.

Johnathan Hale:
    Thank you for your questions. In closing, I'm confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value to our shareholders. We remain focused on strategic priorities, operational excellence, and innovation.

Emily Carter:
    Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our Q3 2024 earnings call. A replay and webcast archive will be available on our investor relations website.

Operator:
    This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
